:::: gw-chapter-intro
::: gw-chapter-intro__body
::: gw-prose
Multi-benefit land repurposing (MLRP) treats farmland facing reduced water
availability under SGMA as an opportunity to deliver habitat, community and
economic benefits alongside water savings, rather than leaving it to fallow
unplanned. Each of those benefits implies a measurement. This chapter asks
which measurements are made, when, and whether they feed the accounting
system.

Four of the {{< var active_basins_word >}} subbasins are covered by a
Department of Conservation MLRP block grant of \$8.89–10 million. They differ
most in when they count water: after implementation, before it, or not as a
separate figure at all. None measures a delivered outcome for the co-benefits
it names. Colusa and Yolo hold no MLRP grant. Their repurposing-type activity
happens through other programs and partners.
:::
:::

```{=html}
<h2 class="gw-eyebrow">Beyond water savings</h2>
<p class="gw-section-lede">How far does quantification reach for each benefit a repurposing program claims? The literature quantifies most of them. In the grantee subbasins, most stop at naming or scoring a benefit before the project is built.</p>

<div id="mlrp-matrix" class="gw-mx gw-loading">Loading the co-benefits matrix&hellip;</div>
<script type="module" src="assets/js/mlrp-matrix.js"></script>

<p class="gw-caption">Measurement states are the analyst's ordinal scale of how far quantification reaches. They are not a score of program quality. "Not found" means not found in the reviewed documents, not that the practice does not exist. Colusa and Yolo hold no MLRP grant and are not rated. Their programs are compared under topic 2.10 below.</p>
```
:::
